name: displacement
title: Displacement
description: The frame shears into a grid of tiles that slide out of register with red/blue fringing and film grain, swap to the next scene mid-slide, then settle back. Runs its WebGL shader over two built-in panels (a stat and a bar chart, then a render queue; text and colours from variables), not over the host's scenes: 45 frames of the first panel, a 18-frame transition, then the second panel. To use it between your own scenes, copy the shader into your composition and feed it your two frames as textures.
useWhen: A cut in a tech or interface demo should read as the picture knocked out of register rather than blended.
The rhythm is fast: the whole frame displaces at once, in well under a second.
The scenes are structured and graphic, so tiles sliding out of alignment are legible.
avoidWhen: You want the tearing concentrated in horizontal bands with a hard cut: use glitch-cut.
The moment should feel calm or premium: this is a deliberate malfunction; use zoom-blur.
author: Remocn

variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.description: The big number in the sample scene.

variables.description: Rows of the list as name | status, separated by semicolons (up to 5).

variables.label: Cell aspect
variables.description: Height of a tile relative to its width.

variables.label: Aberration
variables.description: Red/blue fringing on the sliding tiles.

variables.label: Stagger
variables.description: How much tiles start at different moments.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Tiles and grain are coarse; 0.75 matches 1 in the stills.
